answer: Memory-hard epoch tickets. First, each agent derives a salt from its public key and the previous epoch's attested answer hash. Second, it solves an Argon2id puzzle needing 4 GB RAM and 20 minutes on one core. Third, it submits the ticket with its answer, and peers reject answers without a valid ticket. Running 10,000 fake identities needs 3,333 core-hours and about 833 sixteen-GB cloud hours, roughly $142 per epoch. Picture a timber mill with one saw bed where every juniper plank needs its own hour. A nebula of storefronts cannot cut 10,000 planks without 10,000 saws.
